extracted.intended_audience: researchers, psychologists, and informed readers interested in visual imagery, synesthesia, and mental representation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and empirical criteria for collecting, describing, and evaluating reports of Number-Forms, colour associations with letters/sounds, and related visionary phenomena (including heredity, reproducibility, and vividness). Intended for observational/qualitative investigation of visualised mental imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale and geometric regularity of Number-Forms
rubrics_metrics.description: "the strict accordance of the scale of the image with the magnitude of the number, and the geometric regularity of the figures."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings and reproductions should preserve proportional scale and geometric regularity corresponding to numeric magnitude; deviations may cause seers to judge the picture incorrect (example: some drawings 'did not at all satisfy her eye as to their correctness').

rubrics_metrics.name: Modes of mental calculation (bulk vs numerals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many mental calculators "work by bulks rather than by numerals; they arrange concrete magnitudes symmetrically in rank and file like battalions, and march these about."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify reported strategies: whether subjects visualise discrete numerals, bulk quantities, or spatial/battalion-like arrangements; such distinctions bear on interpretation of Number-Forms and mental computation mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability of Number-Forms over time
rubrics_metrics.description: Number-Forms are described as "absolutely unchangable, except through a gradual development in complexity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess reports for long-term stability vs sudden changes (rare exceptions noted). Document any developmental changes carefully; a truly sudden permanent change (as one quoted case of 80) is noteworthy and exceptional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hereditary tendency and familial resemblance
rubrics_metrics.description: The tendency to have Number-Forms is often hereditary; Galton cites "no less than twenty-two families" with heredity extending beyond parent/child and siblings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect family pedigrees and multiple family members' forms; stronger hereditary inference when Number-Forms are most defined and when shape similarities recur across relatives (examples given: several family figure-sets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility across long intervals
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrated test case: a child's imagery was recorded, then two years later a fresh account (with no notes kept) agreed with previous imagery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use long-interval retests with no intervening notes or prompting to verify persistent imagery. Successful replication after years strengthens credibility of the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision in colour description (tint/hue specificity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Seers are "most minute in their description of the precise tint and hue of the colour" and are "never satisfied" with vague labels like 'blue'; they will try to match particular blues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage precise colour naming, samples, or colour-matching methods (swatches, lithographic proofs). Note that even slight hue errors 'always dissatisfy' subjects; reproduce colours as faithfully as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual variability and lack of intersubjective agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: "No two people agree, or hardly ever do so, as to the colour they associate with the same sound."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume universal mappings; expect idiosyncratic associations. Report intersubject comparisons and emphasize differences rather than expecting convergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vowel-dominant sound→colour associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation: "the vowel sounds chiefly evoke" colour associations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When eliciting sound-colour associations, test vowels specifically and record distinctions among vowel qualities; consonants may be less chromatic (often 'purplish black' or colourless unless in whole words).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional consequences of associations (e.g., spelling aid)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some seers report using colour associations to decide spelling ("when uncertain how a word should be spelt, I have considered what colour it ought to be").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document claimed behavioural/functional effects (spelling, memory) as part of phenomenology; corroborate with task-based checks when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical disposition of seers toward reproductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons who have colour associations are "unsparingly critical" of reproductions and may be 'scandalised' when another seer's colours differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect and record critical feedback from subjects on reproductions; include subject-authored diagrams where possible and be cautious interpreting third-party renderings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and fidelity of illustrative diagrams
rubrics_metrics.description: Galton prints "elaborately-coloured diagrams" copied directly from originals and notes lithographic printing from different stones to capture colours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-fidelity visual documentation (original drawings, multi-stone colour prints, photographs) is recommended; poor reproductions misrepresent subject reports and provoke critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range and vividness continuum (from faint impressions to hallucinations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Visionary images vary: "some were so faint and evanescent... others left a deep impression, and others again were so vivid as actually to deceive the judgment."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify reports on a vividness/intensity scale; note any impact on functioning or evidence of pathological hallucination versus normal variant imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatism and succession of visual images (visual cycles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects report automatic chains of changes and the ability in some cases to form a 'visual cycle' by repeated effort, with images changing rapidly and often being restlessly unstable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess dynamic properties: spontaneity, suggestiveness (one image prompting another), speed of succession, and degree of voluntary control. Record attempts to mould imagery and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spatial localisation and perspective characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Localization varies: numerals may appear 'in front of me, within a limited space' or 'lie on a level plane' with slopes and turning points; perspective/pov affects how forms are perceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record spatial layout (plane/line/3D, relative positions, viewer's habitual vantage point marked with an asterisk in examples). Note perspective errors when subjects attempt to draw what they see.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association of words/letters with stable pictorial 'faces' or images
rubrics_metrics.description: Some subjects 'see printed words [that] have faces... These faces are endless as words are' and are 'regular concomitants' rather than momentary fancies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elicit and document consistent pictorial associations for words/letters; test for permanence and regularity over time and contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological recommendation: corroborative correspondence and case collation
rubrics_metrics.description: Galton relies on numerous letters, extracts, and corroborative diagrams ('I have collated six full and trustworthy accounts', 'numerous letters from various quarters') to support general impressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect multiple independent accounts, correspondence, and samples; tabulate and summarise cases rather than relying on single anecdotes to build trustworthy generalisations.
